entries.clue: Brute with good heart mentioning trump card (5,7)

indicators.note: to mention is to say, so the piece is what you hear

blocks.note: to ruff is to trump in card games
any card of the diamond suit

annotation.surface: A card player praised as a decent sort while slapping down a trump.
annotation.walkthrough: A rough diamond is a coarse-mannered person who is kind underneath. Only the trump needs saying: RUFF, the card-table word for trumping, sounds like ROUGH.
annotation.definitionFit: A rough diamond looks brutish on the outside but has a good heart.

entries.clue: Excellent comprehensive (7)

blocks.note: slang for great, often shortened to 'rad'
comprehensive change goes to the roots, thorough and sweeping

annotation.walkthrough: Two words that look like a school report on a comprehensive school: 'comprehensive' is not the school but thorough, as in radical change.
annotation.definitionFit: Radical is slang for excellent and also means sweeping or thoroughgoing.

entries.clue: European city caught in the rain, those umbrellas initially going up (7)

indicators.note: C, cricket's abbreviation for caught, is held inside THE
take the first letter of each of the words before it
in a down answer, rising means the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: used as it stands, wrapped around C
c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
first letters of rain, those, umbrellas

annotation.surface: Tourists in a continental city put their umbrellas up as the rain starts.
annotation.walkthrough: The assembled string THCERTU is read upwards to give the Dutch city. 'European city' tempts you to look for a hidden word in the rain; nothing is hidden, the pieces are built.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Dutch city is one of many in Europe.

entries.clue: One right to avoid ghastly outlines on title (9)

indicators.note: the one R is left out of the word
the shortened word draws a line around ON, enclosing it

blocks.note: ghastly = horrific; one of its two Rs goes, leaving H…ORIFIC
r = right; one R is removed from HORRIFIC
used as it stands, placed after the H

annotation.surface: A promise to steer clear of gruesome sketches on a book's title page.
annotation.walkthrough: The trap is to read 'on title' as the definition; 'on' is the filling and 'title' alone is the definition, an honorific being a title such as Sir or Dame.
annotation.definitionFit: An honorific is a title of respect, such as Dr or Lady.

entries.clue: First of notes in playing of trio – could it be? (5)

annotation.definition: First of notes in playing of trio – could it be?

indicators.note: take only the first letter of notes
the letters of trio are played about, rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of notes
anagram fodder, 4 letters

annotation.surface: A trio strikes up, and the first notes they play might be the opening.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the first notes a trio plays really are its intro, which is what 'could it be?' flags.
annotation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece, the first notes a band plays.

entries.clue: Soften temper and turn into a Hood’s girl? (7)

blocks.note: to soften temper is to calm someone's anger
a hood is a hoodlum; his girl is his moll, and the suffix -ify means make into

annotation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Hood look like a name, perhaps Robin Hood and Maid Marian; it is a hood, a hoodlum, whose girlfriend is his moll. The question mark owns up to the invented verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: softening someone's temper means calming or appeasing them.

entries.clue: African city near line worker, we hear? (7)

indicators.note: the pieces are to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: nigh = near
a row = a line
the worker bee, crosswords' standard worker

annotation.surface: Someone asks, half-heard, whether an African city lies close to a railway worker.
annotation.walkthrough: Said together, nigh-row-bee is how Nairobi is pronounced, though the spelling shares almost nothing with them.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Kenyan capital is one of Africa's largest cities.

entries.clue: Supporters – four? (4,2,6)

blocks.note: braces are the straps that hold trousers up
a brace is two, so two braces make four

annotation.walkthrough: Braces here are British for what Americans call suspenders. The second definition leans on brace meaning a pair, as in a brace of pheasants; the question mark admits the arithmetic joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are literal: braces hold trousers up, and two braces, each a couple, total four.

entries.clue: Supporter of wood – other golf club too? (7)

blocks.note: and = also, too
wood is one golf club; the other kind is the iron

annotation.surface: A golfer who carries a wood is asked whether the other club comes along as well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wood' reads as a golf club, which is why 'other golf club' follows; in the definition it is firewood, which an andiron holds up in the hearth.
annotation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal stand that supports logs in a fireplace.

entries.clue: First of teams in league scored (7)

indicators.note: take just the first letter of teams

blocks.note: first letter of teams
in league with = allied to

annotation.surface: A report of the leading side in a sports league putting points on the board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'League' pulls towards football tables, but 'in league' means in alliance, and 'scored' means counted up.
annotation.definitionFit: To tally is to count up a score, so tallied means scored.

entries.clue: Enlightening device in linguistics finally grasped by woman failing spelling test? (6,6)

indicators.note: take the last letter of linguistics
the S is held inside the phrase for the woman

blocks.note: a witch not bright enough to pass her spells exam, a dimmer witch
last letter of linguistics, placed between DIMMER and WITCH

annotation.surface: A struggling student of linguistics who keeps failing her spelling tests.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' is not orthography but casting spells, so the failing woman is a less bright witch. 'Enlightening' is literal: the device controls a light.
annotation.definitionFit: A dimmer switch adjusts how much light a lamp gives out, so it is an enlightening device.

entries.clue: Monopoly token that’s unchanged when withdrawn? (7)

indicators.note: drawn backwards, i.e. written in reverse

blocks.note: withdrawn = drawn backwards; a word unchanged by that is a palindrome

annotation.surface: A board-game piece being taken out of play and left just as it was.
annotation.walkthrough: The racing car is one of the classic playing pieces in the board game Monopoly. 'Withdrawn' reads as removed from the board, but it means written backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The racing car is one of the metal tokens players move round a Monopoly board.

entries.clue: Old pro in spirit resembling Humpty Dumpty? (7)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing within another, so FOR sits inside VIM

blocks.note: o = old
vim = energy, spirit; it wraps FOR
pro = for, in favour of

annotation.surface: A veteran professional whose drink leaves him looking like Humpty Dumpty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old pro' looks like one veteran but splits into O and a pro meaning in favour of. Humpty Dumpty is the nursery-rhyme egg, hence egg-shaped.
annotation.definitionFit: Humpty Dumpty is an egg, and oviform means egg-shaped.

entries.clue: Cut twentieth collection of data? (5)

blocks.note: a computer file holds data
count to the twentieth letter of the alphabet and it is T

annotation.surface: A cost-cutting office trims the twentieth set of records.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a verb about trimming data, but it is a noun: a cut of meat or fish. The wordplay reads twentieth before the file; the answer puts it after.
annotation.definitionFit: A filet, or fillet, is a boneless cut of meat or fish.

entries.clue: Over fifty spins – fewer rpm on this? (5-4)

indicators.note: the letters are spun round into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone past fifty spinning old vinyl, perhaps a little slower than they used to.
annotation.walkthrough: A forty-five is a single played at 45 revolutions per minute, fewer than the old 78s. 'Over fifty' pretends to be a number that rules out 45; it is just the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A forty-five is a vinyl single, played at fewer revolutions per minute than a 78.

entries.clue: Change leftist procedure (9)

blocks.note: a red is a left-winger
a course of action, a procedure

annotation.surface: A demand for reform in the way a left-wing group runs things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' sits at the front like a political slogan. Redaction usually means blacking out text, but its older sense is editing or revising.
annotation.definitionFit: A redaction is a revision or edited version of a text, a change made to it.

entries.clue: Provided financial support, or rescued when broke (9)

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone out of money is either bankrolled or bailed out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broke' seems to belong to the money story, penniless, and it is the instruction to break up the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To resource something is to provide it with funds, so resourced means financially supported.

entries.clue: Tennis organisation in hole after elevating one that’s unseeded (7)

indicators.note: LTA goes inside the word for hole
in a down answer, raising the word means reading it upwards

blocks.note: ANUS read upwards; it wraps LTA
the Lawn Tennis Association, Britain's tennis body

annotation.surface: A tennis body lifting an unseeded player out of a hole in the draw.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unseeded' is tennis language for a player without a ranking, but here it means without seeds: a sultana is a seedless dried grape.
annotation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried seedless grape, a fruit with no seeds.

entries.clue: One transported by a super new lift (7)

indicators.note: the I is carried inside the other letters
the letters of 'a super' are made into something new

blocks.note: ASUPER rearranged; it carries the I
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A passenger carried up in a smart new lift.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has you in a lift, so 'lift' seems to belong to the scene, but it is the verb, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: raising something up is lifting it, and both are verbs in the same form.

entries.clue: Half twenty at the outset recalled – as X? (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of twenty
called back, so the string is read in reverse

blocks.note: semi- = half
first letter of twenty

annotation.surface: Someone recalling an old sum where half of twenty came out as a mystery X.
annotation.walkthrough: X here is the multiplication sign, read aloud as times. 'Half twenty' begs to be worked out as ten; it is just SEMI plus a T.
annotation.definitionFit: The symbol X in arithmetic is read as times.

entries.clue: Young sheep stuffed by British artist, full (7)

indicators.note: the young sheep has the artist stuffed into it

blocks.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year; it wraps EMIN
Tracey Emin, the British artist

annotation.surface: A British artist stuffing a lamb for an installation until it is full.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Brit Art's preserved animals. TEG is a crossword regular for a young sheep.
annotation.definitionFit: Teeming means full to overflowing, as in a pond teeming with fish.

entries.clue: Sea creature was a part of someone’s diet, ending on plate (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of plate

blocks.clueFragment: was a part of someone’s diet
blocks.note: read as 'man ate': someone ate it
last letter of plate

annotation.surface: A sea creature once eaten by people, finishing up on a dinner plate.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is read as 'man ate', someone ate it; manatees were in fact once hunted for food, which keeps the surface honest.
annotation.definitionFit: The manatee is a large plant-eating sea mammal, the sea cow.

entries.clue: Measure of food in starter of cheese, or filling in a pork pie (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of cheese
OR is the filling inside the pie

blocks.note: first letter of cheese
a pork pie is rhyming slang for a lie; A LIE wraps OR
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A menu choice between a cheese starter and a slice of pork pie.
annotation.walkthrough: The menu of cheese and pork pie hides rhyming slang: pork pie = lie. 'Starter' and 'filling' sound like cooking and are both instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: A calorie is the unit by which the energy in food is measured.

entries.clue: Ultimate word on efficiency originally drawn up – system clearer? (5)

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above
take the first letter of efficiency
in a down answer, drawing up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
first letter of efficiency

annotation.surface: The final say on streamlining, drafted as a plan to clear out the system.
annotation.walkthrough: 'System clearer' reads as office jargon for streamlining; the system is the digestive one. The question mark marks the definition as playful.
annotation.definitionFit: An enema flushes out the bowels, clearing the body's system.

entries.clue: Asian painter I observed east of cold Asian city (7)

indicators.note: in an across answer, east means to the right, so after C

blocks.note: c = cold, as on a tap
henna, the dye used to paint designs on skin; the first 'Asian' says where it is used
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A report of seeing an Asian artist at work east of some chilly city.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'painter' is no person but henna, the dye used for hand decorations. The clue reads henna and I first, then puts them after C.
annotation.definitionFit: Chennai, formerly Madras, is a major city in south India.

entries.clue: Holiday destination earmarked, where temperature dropped? (7)

indicators.note: the T is let fall out of the word

blocks.note: earmarked = set aside, reserved
t = temperature, removed from SETASIDE

annotation.surface: A holiday resort chosen in advance, then the weather turns cold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temperature dropped' sounds like a weather report ruining the holiday; it is the T falling out of SET ASIDE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the coast is where many British families head for a summer break.

entries.clue: Concerning hearing given to old dictator, ludicrous (7)

indicators.note: 'given to' means handed over and attached, so OTIC is joined on after IDI

blocks.note: Idi Amin, former dictator of Uganda
otic = relating to the ear

annotation.surface: A tyrant granted a court hearing, and the whole thing is absurd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' reads as a court session, but it is the sense of hearing, and OTIC is the medical adjective for the ear.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something foolish enough to laugh at is ludicrous.

entries.clue: Complex realigned given input of retired expert, self-help guru (4,8)

indicators.note: the letters of realigned are made complex, jumbled
the jumbled letters take the reversed expert inside them
gone back, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; it wraps ECA
an ace is an expert; retired, it reads ECA

annotation.surface: A complicated personality, realigned with help from a retired expert, turns into a self-help guru.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complex' sits first as if it were psychology, but it is the anagram signal. Dale Carnegie wrote 'How to Win Friends and Influence People'.
annotation.definitionFit: Dale Carnegie was the American author of 'How to Win Friends and Influence People', the original self-help guru.
